issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Lemma lem:decay uses convexity of $L$ to bound $\langle \nabla L, A\widetilde z_0 - A\wprod \rangle$ by $L(A\widetilde z_0,\y)-L(A\wprod,\y)$. Assumption A3 only requires differentiability and a unique minimum; it does not assume $L(\cdot,\y)$ is convex. Thus the decay inequality and the subsequent convergence claims of Theorem thm:Convergence are not established for nonconvex losses.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis that $L(\cdot,\y)$ (or $L$) is convex to Assumption A3 or directly to Theorem thm:Convergence and its dependents.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence and rate guarantees in Theorem thm:Convergence and all results relying on it are invalid for general losses satisfying only A3.
issues.title: Missing convexity of the loss in the convergence theorem
issues.why_classification: The proof assumes a standard convexity condition that is absent from the formal assumptions. Adding it is a local repair and preserves the intended convergence results, but it narrows the stated scope to convex losses.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem theorem:vector_IRERM requires the limit to satisfy $L(\winfty)=0$ (equivalently $\LossM(\wprod_\infty)=0$). The corollaries only assume the limit exists. They do not assume that the loss attains zero at the limit or that a zero-loss minimizer exists. Hence the conclusion that the limit minimizes over the set $\{\LossM=0\}$ is unsupported; that set can be empty or the limit can be a non-global stationary point.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\LossM(\wprod_\infty)=0$ (or B2 together with a convergence guarantee to a global minimizer) to each corollary before applying Theorem theorem:vector_IRERM.
issues.overall_effect: The implicit-bias characterizations in these corollaries are not established and can be false when the flow does not converge to a global minimizer.
issues.title: Implicit-bias corollaries omit the global-minimizer assumption
issues.why_classification: The corollaries are false as stated because they apply a theorem whose global-minimizer hypothesis is missing. Repairing them requires adding a substantive condition that removes their advertised generality.

issues.failure_explanation: For $\sigmainn=\tanh$, the image of $\R$ is $(-1,1)$, not the closed interval $[-1,1]$ used as $\wDomainRP$ in the trigonometric results. Thus $\tanh\colon\R\to[-1,1]$ is not surjective/invertible, so Assumption A2 as stated is not satisfied. The claim that A2 is easy to check is false for tanh.
